# ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry Weekly Report (Mar 8 - 14, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week, development focused on hardening the Superchain's core infrastructure, specifically targeting derivation pipeline stability and CI reliability. Significant progress was made in auditing error handling to ensure malformed L1 inputs do not disrupt network operations. While the team successfully resolved several long-standing issues related to batch processing and documentation hosting, a critical memory leak involving database read transactions remains a primary concern for node operators on World Chain and other networks.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### CI & Code Generation Improvements
Efforts were made to strengthen the project's automated checks and dependency management to ensure consistency across the codebase.
*   **Enhanced Codegen Detection:** Pull request [#1201](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1201) was opened to expand the `check-codegen` tool, allowing it to detect changes in Go code and dependencies more effectively.
*   **CI Stability:** The daily-codegen CI pipeline was restored by bumping the `op-fetcher` dependency in [#1200](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/pull/1200).

### Protocol Stability & Derivation
The team completed technical audits and refined error-handling logic within the derivation pipeline to prevent chain halts.
*   **Input Error Handling:** A comprehensive audit of the derivation pipeline’s external-input error handling was finalized. This ensures that the system gracefully handles malformed L1 inputs without halting the derivation process ([#19491](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19491)).
*   **Batch Queue Logic:** The team addressed span batch extraction failures in the `BatchQueue`. It was determined that preserving historical behavior for invalid batch data was the safest path forward, as these specific failures have not been observed in production environments ([#19511](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19511)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Documentation Migration:** The hosting of Rust documentation was officially closed as a standalone issue ([#1985](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/1985)), as it has been integrated into the broader documentation migration strategy.
*   **Derivation Pipeline:** Multiple sub-issues related to the derivation pipeline audit were resolved, marking a milestone in protocol security.

### New & Active Issues
*   **Database Memory Leaks:** A high-priority issue ([#19212](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19212)) regarding memory leaks in database read transactions continues to be a major point of discussion. Reports indicate that World Chain v1.10.1 experienced node crashes due to this leak. While some users on v1.10.2 reported temporary stability, the community is currently evaluating whether the v1.11.0 upgrade provides a permanent fix. This remains a potential blocker for stable node operations on high-throughput chains.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week saw active troubleshooting and knowledge sharing between maintainers and node operators. The discussion surrounding the database memory leak ([#19212](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-registry/issues/19212)) highlights a strong collaborative effort to diagnose production issues, with contributors like `0xForerunner` and `jonathanudd` providing critical data points from live environments. Additionally, the resolution of the `BatchQueue` logic demonstrates a pragmatic approach to protocol maintenance, prioritizing production-tested stability over theoretical refactors.
